lists.name: Bedfordshire
lists.description: Bedfordshire is a largely rural county in the East of England, known for rolling farmland, market towns and historic country estates. Bedford and Luton are its main urban centres, with strong connections to London and the wider Midlands.

places.name: Bedford
places.description: A market town on the River Great Ouse in Bedfordshire, historically linked to John Bunyan, author of The Pilgrim's Progress, who was imprisoned here.

places.name: Central Bedfordshire
places.description: A district in Bedfordshire covering a mix of market towns and villages, including Leighton Buzzard and Ampthill, on London's northern commuter fringe.

places.name: Luton
places.description: A town in Bedfordshire historically built on hat-making, today better known as home to London Luton Airport and a diverse, multicultural population.

lists.name: Berkshire
lists.description: Berkshire is a prosperous county west of London, combining attractive countryside with major towns and business centres. It is particularly known for Windsor, the Thames Valley, historic estates and technology companies around Reading and Maidenhead.

places.name: Bracknell Forest
places.description: A district in Berkshire built up substantially as a post-war New Town, with the ancient Windsor Great Park and Swinley Forest woodland nearby.

places.name: Windsor and Maidenhead
places.description: A district in Berkshire home to Windsor Castle, the oldest and largest inhabited castle in the world and a working royal residence.

places.name: Slough
places.description: A large town in Berkshire that grew rapidly as an industrial estate hub from the 1920s, now a diverse, fast-growing commercial centre near Heathrow.

places.name: Reading
places.description: A large town in Berkshire on the Thames and Kennet rivers, known for its major music festival, tech industry presence, and historic abbey ruins.

places.name: West Berkshire
places.description: A large rural district in Berkshire covering the market town of Newbury, known for its racecourse and the rolling North Wessex Downs.

places.name: Wokingham
places.description: An affluent commuter town in Berkshire, historically a centre for silk weaving, now known for its Georgian high street and leafy surrounding countryside.

lists.name: Best London Viewpoints
lists.description: Rooftops, hilltops and bridges…

places.name: Primrose Hill
places.description: Panoramic view over the city…

lists.name: Bristol
lists.description: Bristol is a ceremonial county centred on the historic city of Bristol in South West England. The city is a major cultural, economic and educational centre, known for its harbour, creative industries, engineering heritage and distinctive Georgian and Victorian architecture.

places.name: City of Bristol
places.description: A major port city and unitary authority in the West of England, famous for its maritime trading history, the Clifton Suspension Bridge, and a fiercely independent creative and music culture. Once central to the transatlantic slave trade, a history the city has increasingly confronted in recent years.

lists.name: Buckinghamshire
lists.description: Buckinghamshire is a largely rural and affluent county north-west of London, characterised by rolling Chiltern countryside, historic villages and market towns. It includes places such as Aylesbury, High Wycombe and Milton Keynes, with strong transport and economic links to London.

places.name: Aylesbury Vale
places.description: A rural district in Buckinghamshire named for the fertile Vale of Aylesbury, home to the county town of Aylesbury and close to Waddesdon Manor, a lavish Rothschild estate.

places.name: Chiltern
places.description: A former district in Buckinghamshire covering the Chiltern Hills' beech woodlands and the towns of Amersham and Chesham.

places.name: Milton Keynes
places.description: A planned New Town in Buckinghamshire built from 1967, known for its grid-system roads, extensive parkland, and iconic concrete cow sculptures.

places.name: South Bucks
places.description: A former affluent, rural district in Buckinghamshire near the Thames, covering villages close to Slough and Burnham Beeches ancient woodland.

places.name: Wycombe
places.description: A former district in Buckinghamshire centred on High Wycombe, historically the centre of England's furniture-making industry, particularly Windsor chairs.

lists.name: Cambridgeshire
lists.description: Cambridgeshire is a predominantly flat county in the East of England, famous for its fenlands, waterways and agricultural landscape. Cambridge is its principal city and an internationally renowned centre for education, science, technology and research.

places.name: East Cambridgeshire
places.description: A rural district covering the cathedral city of Ely, whose Norman cathedral rises dramatically above the flat Fenland landscape, nicknamed 'the Ship of the Fens.'

places.name: Cambridge
places.description: A university city on the River Cam, world-famous for its historic colleges, chapel architecture, and the tradition of punting along the Backs behind King's College.

places.name: South Cambridgeshire
places.description: A rural district ringing Cambridge city, made up of villages and farmland, with the American Cemetery at Madingley among its notable sites.

places.name: Fenland
places.description: A flat, rural district in Cambridgeshire covering the Fens, reclaimed marshland now some of England's most fertile farmland, and the market town of Wisbech.

places.name: Huntingdonshire
places.description: A district in Cambridgeshire around the market town of Huntingdon, birthplace of Oliver Cromwell, with the riverside town of St Ives nearby.

places.name: Peterborough
places.description: A cathedral city in Cambridgeshire with a striking Norman cathedral at its centre, transformed into a major New Town in the 1960s and now a growing commercial hub.

lists.name: Causeway Coast Way
lists.description: The Causeway Coast Way is a premier 33-mile (53 km) long-distance trail tracing Northern Ireland’s rugged northern shoreline from Portstewart to Ballycastle. Widely celebrated for its dramatic coastal scenery, the route weaves past sweeping sand dunes, chalk cliffs, historic seaside towns, and centuries-old castle ruins perched precariously over the North Atlantic.

badge.name: Causeway Coast Way
badge.description: Walk the full Causeway Coast Way.

lists.name: Cheshire
lists.description: Cheshire is a historic county in North West England known for its attractive countryside, agricultural landscapes and affluent villages and towns. It includes Chester and major settlements such as Crewe and Warrington, alongside historic estates and parts of the Peak District fringe.

places.name: Cheshire East
places.description: A district covering much of eastern Cheshire, including the historic town of Macclesfield and the market town of Nantwich, known for its Tudor black-and-white architecture and dairy farming heritage.

places.name: Cheshire West and Chester
places.description: A district covering the Roman walled city of Chester, with its distinctive black-and-white Tudor 'Rows' shopping galleries and a well-preserved medieval street plan.

places.name: Halton
places.description: A district in Cheshire covering the towns of Runcorn and Widnes, historically a centre of the chemical industry on the banks of the River Mersey.

places.name: Warrington
places.description: An industrial town in Cheshire on the River Mersey, historically a centre for wire and chemical manufacturing, now a growing commercial hub between Liverpool and Manchester.

lists.name: City of London
lists.description: City of London is a tiny ceremonial county at the historic heart of London, covering the ancient financial district known as the Square Mile. It is one of the world's leading financial centres, dominated by offices, historic churches and landmarks such as St Paul's Cathedral.

places.name: City of London
places.description: The historic square-mile financial district at London's core, governed separately from the rest of the city since medieval times, blending ancient churches with skyscrapers like the Gherkin.

lists.name: Cornwall
lists.description: Cornwall is a distinctive coastal county at the south-western tip of England, famous for dramatic cliffs, sandy beaches and rugged moorland. Its Celtic heritage, fishing communities, tourism and strong regional identity make it one of England's most recognisable counties.

places.name: Cornwall
places.description: England's southwesternmost county, a peninsula of dramatic Atlantic coastline, fishing villages, and a distinct Celtic identity with its own language. Home to St Michael's Mount, the Eden Project, and some of Britain's best surfing beaches.

lists.name: County Durham
lists.description: County Durham is a county in North East England centred on the historic city of Durham and its cathedral. It combines a largely rural interior and former mining communities with more urban areas along the River Wear and Tees.

places.name: County Durham
places.description: A large rural county in northeast England, home to Durham Cathedral, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the finest examples of Norman architecture in Europe.

places.name: Darlington
places.description: A market town in County Durham with a well-preserved Victorian centre, historically a railway engineering hub as the birthplace of the Stockton and Darlington Railway.

places.name: Hartlepool
places.description: A historic port town on the northeast coast, with maritime roots stretching back to a 7th-century monastery, now home to the National Museum of the Royal Navy's HMS Trincomalee.

lists.name: Cumberland
lists.description: Cumberland is a ceremonial county in north-west England created in the 2023 local government reorganisation. It covers much of the western part of the former Cumbria area, including Carlisle and the Solway Coast, with the Lake District forming a major part of its landscape.

places.name: Allerdale District
places.description: A district on Cumbria's northwest coast bordering the Lake District National Park, including the town of Keswick and Derwentwater, one of the region's most photographed lakes.

places.name: Carlisle
places.description: The historic border city of Cumbria, shaped for centuries by conflict between England and Scotland, with a Norman castle and cathedral still standing at its core.

places.name: Copeland
places.description: A coastal district on Cumbria's west coast, home to the market town of Whitehaven and the Sellafield nuclear site, with the western fells of the Lake District rising just inland.

lists.name: Derbyshire
lists.description: Derbyshire is a county in the East Midlands known for its varied countryside, including the dramatic landscapes of the Peak District. Derby is its principal city, while towns such as Chesterfield and Buxton reflect the county's industrial and market-town heritage.

places.name: Amber Valley
places.description: A district in Derbyshire named for the River Amber, covering former mill and mining towns including Belper, a UNESCO World Heritage mill town on the Derwent.

places.name: Erewash
places.description: A district in Derbyshire covering the towns of Ilkeston and Long Eaton, historically tied to lace-making and the East Midlands' industrial rail network.

places.name: Bolsover
places.description: A district in Derbyshire named for its dramatic 17th-century castle overlooking former coalfield towns, now reclaimed for green space.

places.name: Chesterfield
places.description: A market town in Derbyshire famous for the twisted spire of its parish church, said to have been warped by either a devil's curse or simple medieval carpentry error.

places.name: Derby
places.description: An industrial city in Derbyshire long associated with Rolls-Royce aero engines and railway engineering, with roots in the world's first factory, Lombe's Silk Mill, built in 1721.

places.name: Derbyshire Dales
places.description: A district covering much of the Peak District's limestone dale country, including the spa town of Matlock Bath and the historic village of Bakewell, famous for its tart.

places.name: High Peak
places.description: A district in Derbyshire covering the dramatic gritstone edges and moorland of the northern Peak District, including the towns of Buxton and Glossop.

places.name: North East Derbyshire
places.description: A rural district in Derbyshire on the Peak District's eastern edge, covering former mining villages and market towns like Clay Cross.

places.name: South Derbyshire
places.description: A largely rural district in southern Derbyshire, home to the National Forest and the market town of Swadlincote, with a landscape shaped by former coalfields now reclaimed for woodland and leisure.

lists.name: Devon
lists.description: Devon is a large South West county characterised by rolling farmland, two dramatic coastlines, moorland and historic towns. Exeter and Plymouth are its main urban centres, while Dartmoor and Exmoor provide some of England's most distinctive upland landscapes.

places.name: East Devon
places.description: A district of red cliffs and Jurassic Coast heritage in Devon, including the Regency seaside town of Sidmouth alongside the cathedral city of Exeter's eastern neighbours.

places.name: Exeter
places.description: A cathedral city in Devon with roots stretching back to Roman Britain, centred on its Gothic cathedral and a compact, walkable historic core. A regional hub for the South West, with a well-regarded university.

places.name: Mid Devon
places.description: A rural district in Devon centred on the market town of Tiverton, with rolling farmland and the Grand Western Canal running through it.

places.name: North Devon
places.description: A rugged, rural district on Devon's Atlantic coast, home to the surf town of Woolacombe, the historic port of Barnstaple, and Exmoor's western reaches. Known for dramatic cliffs and some of England's best surfing beaches.

places.name: Plymouth
places.description: A major naval port city in Devon from which the Pilgrims set sail for America in 1620, with a history deeply tied to explorers like Sir Francis Drake.

places.name: South Hams
places.description: A rural district in south Devon covering the fishing town of Salcombe and the countryside of the South Hams, a favourite sailing destination.

places.name: Teignbridge
places.description: A district in south Devon covering the Georgian resort town of Teignmouth, the market town of Newton Abbot, and a stretch of Dartmoor National Park's eastern edge.

places.name: Torbay
places.description: The 'English Riviera' on Devon's south coast, made up of the resort towns of Torquay, Paignton, and Brixham, known for palm-lined promenades and a mild microclimate.

places.name: Torridge
places.description: A rural district in North Devon covering the market town of Bideford and dramatic Atlantic coastline near Hartland Point.

places.name: West Devon
places.description: A rural district covering much of Dartmoor National Park's western side, including the market town of Tavistock, birthplace of Sir Francis Drake.

lists.name: Dorset
lists.description: Dorset is a predominantly rural county on England's south coast, famous for its Jurassic Coast, rolling chalk hills and picturesque villages. Bournemouth, Poole and Weymouth provide major coastal urban centres, while the countryside has a strong agricultural and tourism economy.

places.name: Bournemouth
places.description: A classic Victorian seaside resort on England's south coast, known for its wide sandy beach, pine-lined chines, and lively nightlife around the town centre. Merged with Poole and Christchurch into a single unitary authority in 2019.

places.name: Christchurch
places.description: A historic town in Dorset named for its Norman priory church, the longest parish church in England, sitting where the Avon and Stour rivers meet the sea.

places.name: Poole
places.description: A historic harbour town on England's south coast, home to one of the largest natural harbours in the world. Known for Sandbanks' expensive waterfront, Brownsea Island (birthplace of the Scout movement), and a Blue Flag beach that regularly ranks among Britain's best.

places.name: East Dorset
places.description: A former rural district in Dorset covering market towns like Wimborne Minster, home to a striking medieval minster church with a chained library.

places.name: North Dorset
places.description: A rural district of rolling chalk downs and market towns in Dorset, including Blandford Forum's Georgian streets and the ancient hillfort of Hambledon Hill.

places.name: Purbeck
places.description: A rural district in Dorset covering the dramatic Jurassic Coast around Lulworth Cove and the Isle of Purbeck, home to Corfe Castle's ruins.

places.name: West Dorset
places.description: A rural district covering the rolling hills and Jurassic Coast fringes of west Dorset, including the market town of Bridport and the fossil-famous seaside town of Lyme Regis. Known for dramatic coastline, thatched villages, and a slower pace of English countryside life.

places.name: Weymouth and Portland District
places.description: A Georgian seaside resort in Dorset, a favourite of King George III, with the dramatic limestone Isle of Portland forming the southern tip of Chesil Beach.

lists.name: East Riding of Yorkshire
lists.description: East Riding of Yorkshire is a largely rural county surrounding Hull and stretching from the Yorkshire Wolds to the North Sea coast. It is known for fertile agricultural land, dramatic coastal scenery and historic market towns such as Beverley.

places.name: East Riding of Yorkshire
places.description: A large rural district covering the Yorkshire Wolds' chalk hills and coastal towns, with the historic market town of Beverley at its heart.

places.name: City of Kingston upon Hull
places.description: A port city on the Humber estuary, historically built on fishing and maritime trade, and birthplace of anti-slavery campaigner William Wilberforce.

lists.name: East Sussex
lists.description: East Sussex is a county on the south coast of England known for its chalk landscapes, historic towns and coastline. Brighton and Hove is its largest urban centre, while the South Downs, Seven Sisters and towns such as Lewes and Hastings define much of its character.

places.name: Wealden
places.description: A large rural district in East Sussex covering the Ashdown Forest, inspiration for A.A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh, and the historic town of Battle, site of the 1066 Norman Conquest.

places.name: Brighton and Hove
places.description: A vibrant seaside city on the East Sussex coast, known for its Regency architecture, the exotic Royal Pavilion, and one of Britain's most famous LGBTQ+ communities.

places.name: Eastbourne
places.description: A genteel Victorian seaside resort on the East Sussex coast, known for its long promenade, pier, and proximity to the chalk cliffs of Beachy Head, one of England's most dramatic coastal viewpoints.

places.name: Hastings
places.description: A historic town on the East Sussex coast, forever linked to the 1066 Battle of Hastings fought just inland, with a fishing quarter of distinctive tall wooden net huts.

places.name: Lewes
places.description: A historic county town in East Sussex famous for its dramatic Bonfire Night celebrations, a Norman castle, and a compact, hilly high street of independent shops.

places.name: Rother
places.description: A rural district in East Sussex covering the historic town of Rye, with its cobbled medieval streets, and stretches of coastline and countryside near Bexhill and Battle. Rich in Cinque Ports and Norman Conquest history.

lists.name: Essex
lists.description: Essex is a large county north-east of London, combining fertile farmland and attractive rural landscapes with rapidly growing towns and major transport corridors. Chelmsford, Colchester and Southend-on-Sea are among its principal urban centres, while the county's proximity to London strongly influences its economy.

places.name: Thurrock
places.description: A district in Essex along the Thames Estuary, home to the Lakeside shopping centre and the Dartford Crossing linking Essex to Kent.

places.name: Basildon
places.description: A New Town in Essex built from the 1940s, now one of the county's largest towns, on the Thames Estuary's northern shore.

places.name: Braintree
places.description: A rural district in Essex covering the market town of Braintree, historically known for silk weaving thanks to the Courtauld family's mills.

places.name: Brentwood
places.description: A commuter town in Essex on the edge of London's green belt, historically a coaching stop on the road from London to East Anglia.

places.name: Castle Point
places.description: A district in Essex on the Thames Estuary, covering the towns of Canvey Island and Benfleet, with a landscape shaped by 20th-century sea defences and flood history.

places.name: Chelmsford
places.description: The county town of Essex, granted city status in 2012, historically a centre for radio and electronics innovation with Marconi's early wireless work.

places.name: Colchester
places.description: Britain's oldest recorded town, founded as the Roman capital Camulodunum, with extensive Roman walls and a Norman castle built atop a Roman temple's foundations.

places.name: Epping Forest
places.description: A district in Essex named for the ancient royal hunting forest at its heart, alongside the town of Loughton on London's northeastern fringe.

places.name: Harlow
places.description: A New Town in Essex built after WWII as one of Britain's first planned 'garden cities,' known for its public sculpture collection and modernist town planning.

places.name: Maldon
places.description: A historic town in Essex on the Blackwater Estuary, known for Maldon sea salt, traditional Thames sailing barges, and the site of the 991 AD Battle of Maldon.

places.name: Rochford
places.description: A district in Essex along the Thames Estuary, covering the town of Rayleigh and Southend Airport, with marshland and countryside toward the coast.

places.name: Southend-on-Sea
places.description: A classic Essex seaside resort on the Thames Estuary, home to the world's longest pleasure pier, stretching well over a mile out to sea.

places.name: Tendring
places.description: A coastal district in Essex covering the resort town of Clacton-on-Sea and the historic 'Sunshine Coast,' including the pretty village of Manningtree.

places.name: Uttlesford
places.description: A rural district in Essex covering Stansted Airport and the historic wool town of Saffron Walden, known for its maze of medieval streets.

lists.name: Gloucestershire
lists.description: Gloucestershire is a county in South West England known for the Cotswolds, the Forest of Dean and the Severn Valley. Gloucester and Cheltenham are its principal urban centres, alongside numerous historic villages and market towns.

places.name: Cheltenham
places.description: A Regency spa town in Gloucestershire known for its elegant white-stucco architecture, the Cheltenham Festival horse racing, and its famous literature and jazz festivals.

places.name: Cotswold
places.description: A district covering the heart of the Cotswolds Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty in Gloucestershire, famous for honey-coloured limestone villages like Bourton-on-the-Water and Bibury.

places.name: Forest of Dean
places.description: A rural district in Gloucestershire named for its ancient royal forest, one of England's few surviving medieval woodlands with a distinct dialect and mining heritage.

places.name: Gloucester
places.description: A cathedral city in Gloucestershire on the River Severn, with a Norman cathedral whose cloisters were used as filming locations for the Harry Potter films.

places.name: South Gloucestershire
places.description: A district on Bristol's northern edge, combining suburban towns like Yate with rural countryside toward the Cotswolds.

places.name: Stroud
places.description: A market town district in Gloucestershire's Cotswolds, known for its independent, artsy character, converted wool mills, and the surrounding 'Five Valleys' countryside.

places.name: Tewkesbury
places.description: A market town in Gloucestershire at the confluence of the Severn and Avon rivers, home to a magnificent Norman abbey and the site of a decisive 1471 Wars of the Roses battle.

lists.name: Greater Manchester
lists.description: Greater Manchester is a metropolitan county in North West England centred on Manchester and surrounded by a dense network of towns and cities. It is one of Britain's major economic and cultural regions, with a strong industrial heritage and an increasingly diversified modern economy.

places.name: Oldham
places.description: A former cotton-spinning town in Greater Manchester that was once the most productive cotton-milling town in the world, its Victorian mill architecture still a defining feature.

places.name: Wigan
places.description: A former coal-mining town in Greater Manchester, its identity shaped by centuries of mining, textiles, and a resilient working-class culture.

places.name: Bolton
places.description: A former cotton-spinning town in Greater Manchester, home to Bolton Wanderers football club and Smithills Hall, one of the oldest manor houses in the North West.

places.name: Bury
places.description: A market town in Greater Manchester famous for its indoor market and black pudding, with a strong textile and papermaking industrial past.

places.name: Manchester
places.description: A major Northern English city that drove the Industrial Revolution as the world's first industrialised city, today known for its music scene, football rivalry, and vibrant Northern Quarter.

places.name: Rochdale
places.description: A former cotton-milling town in Greater Manchester, birthplace of the Co-operative Movement, founded here by the Rochdale Pioneers in 1844.

places.name: Salford
places.description: A city in Greater Manchester on the banks of the River Irwell, transformed from industrial docklands into MediaCityUK, now home to BBC and ITV studios at Salford Quays.

places.name: Stockport
places.description: A town in Greater Manchester famous for its Victorian railway viaduct, one of the largest brick structures in Europe, and its historic hatting industry.

places.name: Tameside
places.description: A district in Greater Manchester made up of former mill towns including Ashton-under-Lyne and Stalybridge, shaped by the cotton industry and the Pennine hills at its eastern edge.

places.name: Trafford
places.description: A district in Greater Manchester covering Old Trafford, home to Manchester United's stadium, and the Imperial War Museum North.

lists.name: Hadrian’s Wall Path
lists.description: The Hadrian’s Wall Path is an iconic 84-mile (135 km) National Trail spanning coast-to-coast across Northern England from Wallsend in Newcastle upon Tyne to Bowness-on-Solway in Cumbria. Following the line of Emperor Hadrian's 2nd-century Roman frontier, it is the only National Trail built along an entire UNESCO World Heritage Site.

badge.name: Hadrian's Wall Path
badge.description: Walk the full Hadrian's Wall Path.

lists.name: Hampshire
lists.description: Hampshire is a large county on the south coast of England, combining extensive countryside with major urban centres and important ports. Winchester, Southampton and Portsmouth are its principal centres, while the New Forest and South Downs provide much of its distinctive landscape.

places.name: Portsmouth
places.description: A naval city on Hampshire's south coast, home to the Royal Navy's historic dockyard, HMS Victory, and the Spinnaker Tower overlooking the harbour.

places.name: Fareham
places.description: A market town in Hampshire on the Solent coast, historically a strawberry-growing centre and gateway to the naval heritage of Portsmouth harbour.

places.name: Basingstoke and Deane
places.description: A commercial town in Hampshire that grew rapidly from the 1960s as an overspill town for London, alongside rural villages in the surrounding Deane.

places.name: East Hampshire
places.description: A rural district in Hampshire covering part of the South Downs National Park and the market town of Petersfield, known for rolling chalk downland.

places.name: Eastleigh
places.description: A town in Hampshire that grew rapidly around its railway works, sitting close to Southampton Airport.

places.name: Gosport
places.description: A naval town on Hampshire's Solent coast, directly across the water from Portsmouth, with a history deeply tied to the Royal Navy — including submarine heritage at the Explosion Museum and HMS Alliance.

places.name: Hart
places.description: A district in Hampshire around the town of Fleet, largely affluent and residential, sitting between the Surrey border and Hampshire's rural heartland.

places.name: Havant
places.description: A borough on Hampshire's south coast, bordering Portsmouth and looking out over Langstone and Chichester Harbours. A mix of Georgian market-town streets in Havant itself and the seaside resort feel of neighbouring Hayling Island.

places.name: New Forest
places.description: A district in Hampshire built around the ancient royal hunting forest of the same name, now a National Park known for free-roaming ponies, heathland, and picturesque villages like Beaulieu.

places.name: Rushmoor
places.description: A district in Hampshire covering the towns of Aldershot and Farnborough, both long associated with the British Army and aviation history.

places.name: Southampton
places.description: A major port city in Hampshire from which the Titanic set sail in 1912, with a history stretching back to Roman and medieval trading days.

places.name: Test Valley
places.description: A rural district in Hampshire named for the River Test, one of England's premier chalk streams for fly fishing, and home to the market town of Andover.

places.name: Winchester
places.description: The ancient capital of Wessex and once of all England under Alfred the Great, a cathedral city known for its Gothic cathedral, Winchester College, and the legendary Round Table on display at the Great Hall.

lists.name: Herefordshire
lists.description: Herefordshire is a predominantly rural county on the Welsh border, characterised by rolling hills, orchards, farmland and historic villages. Hereford is the principal settlement, and the county is particularly associated with cider production, agriculture and the River Wye.

places.name: Herefordshire
places.description: A rural county on the Welsh border known for cider-making, black-and-white timbered villages, and Hereford Cathedral, home to the Mappa Mundi, a medieval map of the known world.

lists.name: Hertfordshire
lists.description: Hertfordshire is an affluent county immediately north of London, characterised by attractive countryside, commuter towns and historic market centres. Places such as St Albans, Watford and Hertford have strong connections to London, while the county also hosts significant business and technology industries.

places.name: Dacorum
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire covering the New Town of Hemel Hempstead and the historic canal town of Berkhamsted, with its Norman castle ruins.

places.name: Welwyn Hatfield
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire home to Welwyn Garden City, one of Britain's pioneering planned garden cities from the early 20th century, alongside the historic town of Hatfield.

places.name: Three Rivers
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire named for the Chess, Colne, and Gade rivers, covering the town of Rickmansworth and access to the Chiltern Hills.

places.name: Broxbourne
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire along the Lee Valley, covering the towns of Cheshunt and Hoddesdon on London's northern commuter fringe.

places.name: East Hertfordshire
places.description: A rural district covering the market towns of Hertford and Bishop's Stortford, with countryside stretching toward the Essex border.

places.name: Hertsmere
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire home to Elstree Studios, a historic British film and TV production hub, and the town of Borehamwood.

places.name: North Hertfordshire
places.description: A district covering the historic market town of Hitchin and the garden city of Letchworth, the world's first, planned in 1903.

places.name: St Albans
places.description: A cathedral city in Hertfordshire built on the site of the Roman city of Verulamium, with an abbey marking the martyrdom of Britain's first Christian saint.

places.name: Stevenage
places.description: One of Britain's first post-war New Towns, built in Hertfordshire from 1946 as a model for pedestrian-friendly urban planning.

places.name: Watford
places.description: A commuter town in Hertfordshire on the edge of London, historically a printing and brewing centre, now known for its large shopping centre and football club.

lists.name: Isle of Wight
lists.description: Isle of Wight is an island ceremonial county off England's south coast, separated from Hampshire by the Solent. It is known for its coastal scenery, beaches, sailing heritage and Victorian resorts, with Newport serving as the island's main administrative centre.

places.name: Isle of Wight
places.description: An island county off England's south coast, a popular sailing and holiday destination known for the Needles chalk stacks and Queen Victoria's former residence, Osborne House.

lists.name: Isles of Scilly
lists.description: Isles of Scilly are a small archipelago and ceremonial county approximately 28 miles off the coast of Cornwall. The islands are renowned for their subtropical climate, beaches, wildlife and distinctive island communities, with tourism forming a major part of the local economy.

places.name: Isles of Scilly
places.description: A remote archipelago off Cornwall's tip, England's southwesternmost point, known for a subtropical microclimate, flower farming, and pristine beaches.

lists.name: Kent
lists.description: Kent is a large county in south-east England stretching from the London fringe to the English Channel. Known as the 'Garden of England', it combines orchards and rolling countryside with historic cities, coastal towns and major transport links to continental Europe.

places.name: Ashford
places.description: A market town in Kent that grew rapidly as a rail hub, now a gateway to the Eurostar and the countryside of the Kent Downs.

places.name: Canterbury
places.description: A cathedral city in Kent and the spiritual heart of the Church of England, its cathedral the site of Thomas Becket's 1170 murder and a major medieval pilgrimage destination.

places.name: Dartford
places.description: A town in Kent at the southern end of the Dartford Crossing, with a history stretching back to a key medieval river crossing and pilgrimage route.

places.name: Dover
places.description: A historic port town in Kent famous for its White Cliffs and status as the closest point in England to mainland Europe, just 33km from France.

places.name: Gravesham
places.description: A district in Kent along the Thames Estuary, its main town of Gravesend historically a key stop for ships heading in and out of London's port.

places.name: Maidstone
places.description: The county town of Kent on the River Medway, with a history in papermaking and brewing, and the ruins of a medieval archbishop's palace.

places.name: Medway
places.description: A unitary authority in Kent formed from the historic 'Medway Towns' of Chatham, Rochester, and Gillingham, defined by the River Medway and centuries of naval shipbuilding history at the former Chatham Dockyard.

places.name: Sevenoaks
places.description: An affluent commuter district in Kent, named for its historic town, and home to Knole, one of England's largest houses and a former archbishop's palace set in a medieval deer park.

places.name: Folkestone and Hythe
places.description: A former district covering Kent's Cinque Ports coastline, including Folkestone and the entrance to the Channel Tunnel.

places.name: Swale
places.description: A district in Kent covering the Isle of Sheppey and the historic town of Sittingbourne, with marshland and orchards along the Thames Estuary.

places.name: Thanet
places.description: A district in Kent covering the Isle of Thanet's seaside resorts, including Margate and Broadstairs, both long popular for traditional English seaside holidays.

places.name: Tonbridge and Malling
places.description: A district in Kent covering the historic market town of Tonbridge, with its Norman castle, and the countryside around West Malling.

places.name: Tunbridge Wells
places.description: A spa town in Kent that grew up around a chalybeate spring discovered in 1606, with an elegant Georgian colonnade, the Pantiles, still at its centre.

lists.name: Lancashire
lists.description: Lancashire is a historic county in North West England with a strong industrial and textile heritage. Its landscape ranges from the Lancashire coast and urban towns such as Preston and Blackburn to the Forest of Bowland and rural valleys.

places.name: Pendle
places.description: A district in Lancashire named for Pendle Hill, infamous for the 1612 witch trials that made it one of England's most notorious folklore landmarks.

places.name: Blackburn with Darwen
places.description: A former cotton-milling powerhouse in Lancashire, its skyline still marked by Victorian mill chimneys. Home to Blackburn Cathedral and a strong regional football tradition at Ewood Park.

places.name: Blackpool
places.description: England's classic bucket-and-spade seaside resort, famous for its illuminations, the Blackpool Tower, and Pleasure Beach amusement park.

places.name: Burnley
places.description: A former cotton-mill town in Lancashire's Pennine foothills, its Victorian textile heritage still visible in the mill architecture. Home to Turf Moor, one of English football's oldest grounds.

places.name: Chorley
places.description: A market town in Lancashire known for its flat cakes, its Victorian covered market, and its proximity to the West Pennine Moors.

places.name: Fylde
places.description: A coastal district in Lancashire between Blackpool and the Ribble estuary, mostly flat farmland and small towns like Lytham St Annes, known for its genteel promenade.

places.name: Hyndburn
places.description: A former cotton-weaving town in Lancashire's Hyndburn valley, its mill heritage still visible in the local architecture.

places.name: Lancaster
places.description: A historic city in Lancashire on the River Lune, with a Norman castle that later served as a courthouse and prison, and deep ties to the 18th-century transatlantic trade.

places.name: Preston
places.description: A historic market and mill town in Lancashire, granted city status in 2002, with a guild history stretching back to 1179 and a still-celebrated 'Preston Guild' tradition.

places.name: Ribble Valley
places.description: A rural district in Lancashire around the market town of Clitheroe, known for its rolling countryside, the Forest of Bowland, and views of Pendle Hill, infamous for the 17th-century witch trials.

places.name: Rossendale
places.description: A district in Lancashire's Pennine valleys, its towns like Rawtenstall shaped by the cotton and footwear industries.

places.name: South Ribble
places.description: A district in Lancashire between Preston and the Ribble estuary, largely residential and suburban, with the historic village of Hoghton and its Tudor hall among its notable spots.

places.name: West Lancashire
places.description: A rural, flat agricultural district in Lancashire around the market town of Ormskirk, known for its bulb and vegetable farming.

places.name: Wyre
places.description: A coastal district in Lancashire including the resort town of Fleetwood and stretches of Fylde coast countryside, historically tied to the fishing industry.

lists.name: Leicestershire
lists.description: Leicestershire is a centrally located county in the East Midlands, combining productive farmland with a network of market towns. Leicester is the dominant urban centre, while the county is also known for its multicultural heritage, industrial history and association with the National Forest.

places.name: Melton
places.description: A rural district in Leicestershire centred on Melton Mowbray, famous as the home of the pork pie and a historic centre of Stilton cheese production.

places.name: Hinckley and Bosworth
places.description: A district in Leicestershire named for the market town of Hinckley and the site of the 1485 Battle of Bosworth Field, where Richard III was killed and the Tudor dynasty began.

places.name: Blaby
places.description: A small district in Leicestershire just southwest of Leicester city, largely suburban and semi-rural. Best known locally for Fosse Park, one of the region's largest retail and leisure parks.

places.name: Charnwood
places.description: A district in Leicestershire named for Charnwood Forest, an ancient upland landscape, and home to the university town of Loughborough.

places.name: Harborough
places.description: A rural district in Leicestershire around the market town of Market Harborough, known for its well-preserved Georgian high street.

places.name: Leicester
places.description: A historic city in the East Midlands where the remains of King Richard III were famously discovered beneath a car park in 2012. Home to significant Roman heritage sites and one of Britain's most diverse populations.

places.name: North West Leicestershire
places.description: A district covering former coalfield towns like Coalville alongside the National Forest, and home to East Midlands Airport.

places.name: Oadby and Wigston
places.description: A small suburban district on Leicester's southern edge, largely residential with a mix of Victorian terraces and green space.

lists.name: Lincolnshire
lists.description: Lincolnshire is a large, predominantly rural county in eastern England, characterised by fertile farmland, the Lincolnshire Wolds and an extensive North Sea coastline. Lincoln, Boston and Grantham are among its principal towns, with agriculture remaining important to the local economy.

places.name: Boston
places.description: A market town in Lincolnshire named for St Botolph's, whose towering church spire (locally 'the Stump') can be seen for miles across the flat Fens. The town lent its name to Boston, Massachusetts.

places.name: East Lindsey
places.description: A large rural district in Lincolnshire covering the seaside resort of Skegness and the wolds countryside, known for its flat coastline and traditional English beach holidays.

places.name: Lincoln
places.description: A cathedral city in Lincolnshire with a hilltop Gothic cathedral once the tallest building in the world, and a well-preserved Norman castle holding an original copy of Magna Carta.

places.name: North East Lincolnshire
places.description: A district on the Humber estuary covering Grimsby, once the world's largest fishing port, its docks now diversifying into renewable energy.

places.name: North Kesteven
places.description: A rural district in Lincolnshire south of Lincoln city, characterised by flat farmland, RAF airfield heritage tied to the county's 'Bomber County' legacy, and the market town of Sleaford.

places.name: North Lincolnshire
places.description: A district around the industrial town of Scunthorpe, historically built on steelmaking, with the Humber estuary forming its northern boundary.

places.name: South Holland
places.description: A flat, agricultural district in Lincolnshire named for its Fenland landscape, centred on the market town of Spalding, historically famous for tulip growing.

places.name: South Kesteven
places.description: A district in Lincolnshire centred on the market town of Grantham, birthplace of Margaret Thatcher and Isaac Newton, with Stamford's Georgian stone streets also within its boundary.

places.name: West Lindsey
places.description: A rural district in Lincolnshire centred on the cathedral city of Lincoln's northern outskirts, and the historic market town of Gainsborough on the River Trent.

lists.name: London Boroughs
lists.description: Greater London is the metropolitan county encompassing London and its 32 boroughs, with the City of London forming a separate ceremonial county. It is England's largest urban area and a global centre for finance, culture, government, education and the creative industries.

places.name: Kensington and Chelsea
places.description: London's smallest and one of its wealthiest boroughs, home to the Natural History Museum, Portobello Road Market, and the King's Road.

places.name: Ealing
places.description: A West London borough nicknamed 'Queen of the Suburbs' for its leafy Victorian and Edwardian streets, home to Ealing Studios, one of the world's oldest continuously working film studios.

places.name: Havering
places.description: An outer East London borough with a semi-rural character, including the historic market town of Romford and green belt countryside toward Essex.

places.name: Newham
places.description: An East London borough that hosted the 2012 Olympic Park, home to Stratford's regeneration, the Westfield shopping centre, and one of London's most ethnically diverse populations.

places.name: Barking and Dagenham
places.description: An East London borough with deep working-class roots in the Ford Dagenham car plant, once one of Europe's largest car factories.

places.name: Barnet
places.description: A large North London borough combining suburban character with the historic Barnet Fair and the site of a decisive 1471 Wars of the Roses battle.

places.name: Bexley
places.description: A southeast London borough on the edge of Kent, home to Danson House, an 18th-century Palladian villa, and a mostly suburban, green character.

places.name: Brent
places.description: A northwest London borough home to Wembley Stadium, the national home of English football, and one of the capital's most multicultural populations.

places.name: Bromley
places.description: A large, leafy South London borough, birthplace of Charles Darwin's theories developed at nearby Down House, and one of London's greenest boroughs.

places.name: Camden
places.description: An inner North London borough famous for Camden Market, its punk and music heritage, and the intellectual legacy of Bloomsbury's literary set nearby.

places.name: Croydon
places.description: A large South London borough that grew into a major commercial and transport hub, with striking 1960s-70s tower blocks alongside a historic core around Croydon Minster.

places.name: Enfield
places.description: A North London borough combining suburban streets with historic Forty Hall, a Jacobean mansion, and the site of a former royal armaments factory.

places.name: Greenwich
places.description: A southeast London borough home to the Royal Observatory and the Prime Meridian, the Cutty Sark, and a UNESCO World Heritage maritime quarter.

places.name: Hackney
places.description: An inner-city London borough that transformed from industrial East End grit into one of the capital's most creative, fashionable districts. Home to Broadway Market, Victoria Park, and a nightlife and street-art scene centred on Shoreditch's northern edge.

places.name: Hammersmith and Fulham
places.description: A West London borough combining riverside Fulham with Hammersmith's theatres and the Apollo, one of London's best-known live music venues.

places.name: Haringey
places.description: A North London borough combining the leafy streets of Muswell Hill with Tottenham's football heritage and diverse communities.

places.name: Harrow
places.description: A northwest London borough best known for Harrow School, one of England's most famous public schools, founded in 1572 and set on a hill above the town.

places.name: Hillingdon
places.description: A large West London borough home to Heathrow Airport and the historic market town of Uxbridge.

places.name: Hounslow
places.description: A West London borough home to Kew Gardens' neighbouring areas, Chiswick's riverside, and a large South Asian community around Southall.

places.name: Islington
places.description: An inner North London borough combining Georgian terraces with a lively restaurant and theatre scene along Upper Street.

places.name: Kingston upon Thames
places.description: A southwest London borough centred on a historic market town where several Anglo-Saxon kings were crowned, marked today by the Coronation Stone outside the Guildhall.

places.name: Lambeth
places.description: A South London borough stretching from the South Bank to Brixton, home to the London Eye, the Imperial War Museum, and one of the capital's most historic Caribbean communities centred on Brixton Market.

places.name: Lewisham
places.description: A South London borough with a lively market and strong Caribbean cultural heritage, alongside green space at Blackheath's southern edge.

places.name: Merton
places.description: A South London borough home to Wimbledon and the All England Lawn Tennis Club, host of the world's oldest tennis championship since 1877.

places.name: Redbridge
places.description: An outer East London borough combining suburban streets with Epping Forest's southern reaches and one of London's largest South Asian communities.

places.name: Richmond upon Thames
places.description: London's only borough spanning both banks of the Thames, home to Richmond Park, the capital's largest Royal Park, and Kew Gardens' botanical collections.

places.name: London Borough of Southwark
places.description: A South London borough home to the Shard, Borough Market, and the Tate Modern, spanning some of the capital's most historic riverside districts.

places.name: Sutton
places.description: A South London borough on the capital's southern fringe, largely suburban with the historic Nonsuch Park among its green spaces.

places.name: Tower Hamlets
places.description: An East London borough spanning historic Whitechapel to the modern skyscrapers of Canary Wharf, one of London's most rapidly transformed areas.

places.name: Waltham Forest
places.description: A northeast London borough covering part of Epping Forest and the historic William Morris Gallery, honouring the designer who was born in the area.

places.name: Wandsworth
places.description: A South London borough stretching along the Thames, combining the green expanse of Wandsworth Common with riverside developments at Battersea.

places.name: Westminster
places.description: The London borough at the heart of British government and royalty, home to the Houses of Parliament, Buckingham Palace, and Westminster Abbey.

lists.name: Merseyside
lists.description: Merseyside is a metropolitan county in North West England centred on the River Mersey and the city of Liverpool. It has a strong maritime and industrial heritage and is internationally known for Liverpool's music, football, architecture and cultural influence.

places.name: Knowsley
places.description: A district on Liverpool's eastern edge, home to Knowsley Safari Park and the historic Knowsley Hall, ancestral seat of the Earls of Derby.

places.name: Liverpool
places.description: A major port city on the Mersey famous as the birthplace of The Beatles, with a UNESCO-recognised waterfront and a fiercely proud maritime and musical heritage.

places.name: Sefton
places.description: A coastal district in Merseyside covering the seaside resort of Southport and the dune-backed beaches near Formby, home to a rare red squirrel population.

places.name: St. Helens
places.description: A former glass-manufacturing town in Merseyside, home to Pilkington Glass and a strong rugby league tradition.

places.name: Wirral
places.description: A peninsula in Merseyside between the Mersey and Dee estuaries, combining seaside towns like New Brighton with commuter suburbs facing Liverpool across the water.

lists.name: National Landscapes
lists.description: The 46 National Landscapes (formerly known as Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty) across England, Wales, and Northern Ireland — protected countryside recognised for exceptional natural beauty, from chalk downland to island coastlines.

places.name: Anglesey (Ynys Môn)
places.description: An island National Landscape off North Wales, encircling almost the entire coastline with beaches, seabird colonies, and prehistoric burial chambers.

places.name: Antrim Coast and Glens National Landscape
places.description: A dramatic Northern Ireland coastline of nine glens running down to the sea, with the Antrim Coast Road ranked among the world's great scenic drives.

places.name: Arnside & Silverdale National Landscape
places.description: A small, coastal National Landscape straddling the Lancashire-Cumbria border, known for limestone pavement, ancient woodland, and views across Morecambe Bay's shifting sands.

places.name: Binevenagh National Landscape
places.description: A striking basalt escarpment overlooking the Roe Valley and the north coast, part of the same volcanic geology as the Giant's Causeway.

places.name: Blackdown Hills National Landscape
places.description: A quiet, little-visited National Landscape in Devon and Somerset, characterised by rolling hills, deep wooded combes, and traditional cider orchards.

places.name: Clwydian Range and Dee Valley National Landscape
places.description: A National Landscape of rolling hills and Iron Age hillforts in northeast Wales, extended in 2011 to include the Dee Valley near Llangollen.

places.name: Cannock Chase National Landscape
places.description: England's smallest National Landscape, a former royal hunting forest in Staffordshire now covered in heathland, pine forest, and mountain bike trails.

places.name: Causeway Coast National Landscape
places.description: Home to the Giant's Causeway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site of hexagonal basalt columns formed by volcanic activity 60 million years ago.

places.name: Gower National Landscape
places.description: The very first AONB in the UK, designated in 1956, a small Welsh peninsula famous for Rhossili Bay's sweeping sands, regularly rated among the world's best beaches.

places.name: Llŷn Peninsula
places.description: A remote Welsh peninsula stretching into the Irish Sea, its National Landscape protecting quiet coves, pilgrim history, and views to Snowdonia.

places.name: Chichester Harbour National Landscape
places.description: A tidal estuary National Landscape on the Sussex-Hampshire border, a haven for sailing, wading birds, and quiet waterside villages like Bosham.

places.name: Lagan Valley
places.description: A green corridor following the River Lagan between Belfast and Lisburn, valued as accessible countryside close to Northern Ireland's largest city.

places.name: Mourne Mountains
places.description: A compact granite mountain range in County Down, said to have inspired C.S. Lewis's Narnia, ringed by the historic Mourne Wall.

places.name: Chilterns National Landscape
places.description: A chalk escarpment National Landscape stretching from the Thames near Goring up through Buckinghamshire, known for beech woodlands and red kites reintroduced in the 1990s.

places.name: Cornwall
places.description: Uniquely split into 12 separate sections covering nearly a third of the county, this National Landscape protects dramatic Atlantic coastline, granite moorland, and former mining landscapes.

places.name: Ring of Gullion National Landscape
places.description: A ring-shaped range of hills in County Armagh formed by an ancient volcanic ring dyke, steeped in Irish mythology tied to the legend of Cú Chulainn.

places.name: Cotswolds National Landscape
places.description: The largest National Landscape in England, a belt of honey-coloured limestone hills famous for chocolate-box villages, dry-stone walls, and wool-church architecture.

places.name: Sperrin National Landscape
places.description: Northern Ireland's largest upland area, a remote range of rounded hills straddling Counties Tyrone and Londonderry, historically mined for gold.

places.name: Strangford and Lecale National Landscape
places.description: A landscape of drumlin islands in Strangford Lough merging with the Lecale coastline, home to Mount Stewart's gardens and Game of Thrones filming locations.

places.name: Cranborne Chase National Landscape
places.description: A chalk landscape straddling Dorset, Wiltshire, and Hampshire, characterised by ancient hunting-forest woodland, Bronze Age barrows, and one of England's darkest night skies.

places.name: Dedham Vale National Landscape
places.description: The compact Essex-Suffolk valley immortalised in John Constable's paintings, still recognisable today from the artist's landscapes of the River Stour.

places.name: Dorset National Landscape
places.description: A varied National Landscape covering chalk downland, heathland, and the Jurassic Coast's fossil-rich cliffs, stretching across much of the county.

places.name: East Devon National Landscape
places.description: A coastal and rural National Landscape of red sandstone cliffs and the Jurassic Coast's eastern reaches, including the resort town of Sidmouth.

places.name: Forest of Bowland National Landscape
places.description: A remote, heather-moorland National Landscape in Lancashire, historically a royal hunting ground and near the area associated with the 17th-century Pendle witch trials.

places.name: High Weald
places.description: One of the best-preserved medieval landscapes in northwest Europe, spanning Kent, Sussex, and Surrey with ancient woodland, sunken lanes, and scattered oast houses.

places.name: Howardian Hills National Landscape
places.description: A gentle, wooded National Landscape in North Yorkshire between the Yorkshire Wolds and the North York Moors, dotted with historic estates like Castle Howard.

places.name: Isle of Wight
places.description: England's largest island off the Hampshire coast, its National Landscape covering chalk downs, the Needles rock stacks, and dinosaur-fossil-rich cliffs.

places.name: Isles of Scilly National Landscape
places.description: England's smallest National Landscape, an archipelago 28 miles off Cornwall known for a subtropical microclimate, flower farming, and pristine white-sand beaches.

places.name: Kent Downs
places.description: A chalk ridge running from the White Cliffs of Dover to the Surrey border, nicknamed the 'Garden of England' for its orchards, hop gardens, and vineyards.

places.name: Lincolnshire Wolds National Landscape
places.description: A gently rolling range of chalk hills in Lincolnshire, one of England's least-visited National Landscapes, known for wide skies and quiet villages.

places.name: Malvern Hills National Landscape
places.description: A dramatic ridge of ancient volcanic rock rising abruptly from the Severn plain, long associated with composer Edward Elgar and the source of Malvern spring water.

places.name: Mendip Hills National Landscape
places.description: A limestone plateau in Somerset riddled with caves and gorges, including the dramatic Cheddar Gorge, England's largest gorge.

places.name: Nidderdale National Landscape
places.description: A Yorkshire Dales-adjacent National Landscape following the River Nidder, known for reservoirs, heather moorland, and the curious Brimham Rocks.

places.name: Norfolk Coast National Landscape
places.description: A low-lying coastal National Landscape of salt marshes, dunes, and pine woods, home to seal colonies and some of England's best birdwatching.

places.name: North Devon Coast National Landscape
places.description: A rugged Atlantic coastline National Landscape taking in dramatic cliffs, the surf beaches around Woolacombe, and Exmoor's western fringe.

places.name: North Pennines National Landscape
places.description: England's largest National Landscape, a windswept upland region of moorland and dales sometimes called 'England's last wilderness,' and a UNESCO Global Geopark.

places.name: North Wessex Downs National Landscape
places.description: A chalk downland National Landscape spanning Wiltshire, Berkshire, Hampshire, and Oxfordshire, home to Avebury's prehistoric stone circle.

places.name: Northumberland Coast
places.description: A dramatic stretch of coastline dotted with castles including Bamburgh and Dunstanburgh, backed by wide sandy beaches and dune systems.

places.name: Quantock Hills National Landscape
places.description: England's first ever AONB, designated in 1957, a compact range of wooded hills and heather moorland in Somerset.

places.name: Shropshire Hills National Landscape
places.description: A varied upland National Landscape on the Welsh border, taking in the rocky Stiperstones, the Long Mynd moorland, and Wenlock Edge's wooded scarp.

places.name: Solway Coast National Landscape
places.description: A remote, low-lying National Landscape on Cumbria's northern coast, facing Scotland across the Solway Firth, known for saltmarsh and migratory birdlife.

places.name: South Devon National Landscape
places.description: A National Landscape of drowned river valleys ('rias'), fishing villages, and the South Hams' rolling countryside between Torbay and Plymouth.

places.name: Suffolk & Essex Coast & Heaths National Landscape
places.description: A National Landscape of heathland, reed-fringed estuaries, and shingle beaches along the Suffolk and north Essex coast, including Sutton Hoo's Anglo-Saxon burial ground.

places.name: Surrey Hills
places.description: A wooded, chalk-and-greensand National Landscape on London's doorstep, centred on Box Hill, one of England's most-visited beauty spots.

places.name: Tamar Valley National Landscape
places.description: The most recently designated English National Landscape (1995), following the river that forms the Devon-Cornwall border through former mining and market-garden country.

places.name: Wye Valley National Landscape
places.description: A dramatic gorge landscape straddling England and Wales, carved by the River Wye, overlooked by the ruins of Tintern Abbey.

lists.name: Norfolk
lists.description: Norfolk is a largely rural county in eastern England, famous for its flat agricultural landscapes, Norfolk Broads and extensive coastline. Norwich is the principal city, while coastal resorts and historic market towns contribute to a strong tourism and heritage economy.

places.name: Breckland
places.description: A rural district in Norfolk named for the Brecks, a distinctive sandy heathland landscape, and home to the market town of Thetford.

places.name: Broadland
places.description: A district in Norfolk taking in part of the Norfolk Broads, a network of navigable rivers and lakes popular for boating holidays, just north of Norwich.

places.name: Great Yarmouth
places.description: A traditional English seaside resort on the Norfolk coast, once a major herring fishing port, now known for its beach, pier, and Victorian promenade.

places.name: King's Lynn and West Norfolk
places.description: A district centred on the historic Hanseatic League port of King's Lynn, with a well-preserved medieval merchant quarter and the nearby royal Sandringham Estate.

places.name: North Norfolk
places.description: A coastal district in Norfolk known for its salt marshes, seal colonies, and genteel seaside towns like Cromer and Wells-next-the-Sea.

places.name: Norwich
places.description: A historic cathedral city in Norfolk, one of medieval England's largest and wealthiest, with a Norman cathedral, castle, and a distinctive circular market dating back centuries.

places.name: South Norfolk
places.description: A rural district ringing Norwich, covering market towns like Wymondham with its twin-towered abbey church.

lists.name: North Yorkshire
lists.description: North Yorkshire is England's largest ceremonial county by area, stretching from the Yorkshire Dales and North York Moors to the North Sea coast. It combines spectacular rural landscapes with historic towns and cities such as York, Harrogate and Scarborough.

places.name: York
places.description: A walled cathedral city in North Yorkshire, home to the largest Gothic cathedral in Northern Europe, York Minster, and the best-preserved medieval streets in England, including the Shambles.

places.name: Harrogate
places.description: A genteel Victorian spa town in North Yorkshire, known for its Royal Pump Room, elegant gardens, and reputation as one of Britain's most pleasant places to live.

places.name: Craven
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire covering the market town of Skipton, known as the 'Gateway to the Dales.'

places.name: Hambleton District
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire covering the Vale of York and part of the North York Moors, including the market town of Thirsk, associated with vet-turned-author James Herriot.

places.name: Richmondshire
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire named for the market town of Richmond and its Norman castle, gateway to the Yorkshire Dales.

places.name: Ryedale
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire covering the market town of Malton and the southern edge of the North York Moors, known for its food scene and Castle Howard nearby.

places.name: Middlesbrough
places.description: An industrial town on Teesside built rapidly in the 19th century around iron and steel production, once nicknamed 'Ironopolis.'

places.name: Scarborough
places.description: A traditional Yorkshire seaside resort, often credited as Britain's first seaside holiday town, with a medieval castle overlooking two sweeping bays.

places.name: Selby
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire around the market town of Selby, home to a magnificent Norman abbey and flat farmland toward the Vale of York.

places.name: Stockton-on-Tees
places.description: A town on Teesside straddling the River Tees, historically the starting point of the world's first passenger railway in 1825.

places.name: Redcar and Cleveland
places.description: A coastal borough historically part of Cleveland, combining the seaside resort of Redcar with the industrial legacy of Teesside's steelworks and a stretch of dramatic North Sea coastline.

lists.name: Northamptonshire
lists.description: Northamptonshire is a centrally located county in the East Midlands known for rolling countryside, historic market towns and a long association with shoemaking. Northampton and Kettering are major population centres, while its position near major motorways gives it an important logistics role.

places.name: East Northamptonshire
places.description: A former rural district in Northamptonshire covering market towns like Oundle, known for its well-preserved stone architecture.

places.name: Daventry
places.description: A market town in Northamptonshire with a history as a coaching stop on the road between London and the Midlands, now known for its reservoir and country park.

places.name: Wellingborough
places.description: A market town in Northamptonshire with a long history in the boot and shoe trade, sitting along the River Nene in the county's industrial heartland.

places.name: Corby
places.description: A town in Northamptonshire shaped by 20th-century steelmaking and a strong Scottish immigrant community drawn by industrial jobs, earning it the nickname 'Little Scotland.'

places.name: Kettering
places.description: A market town in Northamptonshire historically tied to the boot and shoe trade, sitting amid rolling countryside near Rockingham Castle.

places.name: Northampton
places.description: The county town of Northamptonshire, historically the centre of England's shoemaking industry, with a heritage still celebrated at the town's shoe museum.

places.name: South Northamptonshire
places.description: A rural district of honey-coloured stone villages in Northamptonshire, home to Silverstone Circuit, the historic home of the British Grand Prix.

lists.name: Northumberland
lists.description: Northumberland is England's northernmost county, stretching from the Scottish border to the North Sea. It is renowned for vast open landscapes, rugged coastline, castles and Hadrian's Wall, with relatively low population density compared with most English counties.

places.name: Northumberland
places.description: England's northernmost county, a vast and sparsely populated landscape of Hadrian's Wall, dramatic coastline, and medieval castles including Alnwick and Bamburgh. One of the best places in England for dark-sky stargazing.

lists.name: Nottinghamshire
lists.description: Nottinghamshire is a county in the East Midlands known for its association with the legend of Robin Hood, Sherwood Forest and the city of Nottingham. It combines a major urban centre with former coalfield communities, agricultural areas and historic market towns.

places.name: Ashfield
places.description: A former coal-mining district in Nottinghamshire, its towns like Hucknall still carrying the legacy of the pits, alongside associations with poet Lord Byron.

places.name: Bassetlaw District
places.description: A district in Nottinghamshire around the market town of Retford, historically linked to the Pilgrim Fathers, several of whom came from villages in this area before sailing for America.

places.name: Broxtowe
places.description: A district in Nottinghamshire on the western edge of Nottingham city, including the town of Beeston and countryside associated with author D.H. Lawrence, who was born nearby.

places.name: Gedling
places.description: A district on Nottingham's eastern edge, largely suburban, taking its name from a former colliery village now redeveloped into a country park.

places.name: Mansfield
places.description: A former coal-mining town in Nottinghamshire, its identity long shaped by the pits, with the Sherwood Forest fringes lying nearby.

places.name: Newark and Sherwood
places.description: A district in Nottinghamshire covering the historic market town of Newark-on-Trent and the legendary Sherwood Forest, home of the Robin Hood legend.

places.name: Nottingham
places.description: A historic city famed for its Robin Hood legend, with a medieval castle, extensive cave network beneath the city, and a strong lace-making heritage.

places.name: Rushcliffe
places.description: An affluent suburban district south of Nottingham, covering West Bridgford and the National Water Sports Centre at Holme Pierrepont.

lists.name: Oxfordshire
lists.description: Oxfordshire is an affluent county in South East England centred on the historic city of Oxford. It is known internationally for the University of Oxford, picturesque countryside and a strong concentration of science, technology and research industries.

places.name: Oxford
places.description: A world-famous university city, home to the oldest university in the English-speaking world, with dreaming spires, historic colleges, and the Bodleian Library dating to 1602.

places.name: West Oxfordshire
places.description: A rural Cotswolds-adjacent district in Oxfordshire home to Blenheim Palace, birthplace of Winston Churchill and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the market town of Witney.

places.name: Cherwell
places.description: A rural district in Oxfordshire covering the market town of Banbury, famous for the nursery rhyme 'Ride a cock-horse to Banbury Cross.'

places.name: South Oxfordshire
places.description: A rural district southeast of Oxford, taking in the Chiltern Hills, the Thames-side town of Wallingford, and the riverside village of Goring.

places.name: Vale of White Horse
places.description: A rural district in Oxfordshire named for the prehistoric Uffington White Horse chalk figure carved into a hillside, alongside the market town of Abingdon.

lists.name: Rutland
lists.description: Rutland is England's smallest ceremonial county, centred on the towns of Oakham and Uppingham. It is predominantly rural and is particularly known for Rutland Water, rolling farmland and its quiet market-town character.

places.name: Rutland
places.description: England's smallest historic county, a compact patchwork of stone villages and farmland centred on Rutland Water, one of the largest reservoirs in Europe and a major spot for birdwatching and sailing.

lists.name: Shropshire
lists.description: Shropshire is a large, predominantly rural county on the Welsh border, known for rolling hills, historic towns and the Shropshire Hills. Shrewsbury is the principal town, while Telford provides the county's largest modern urban and industrial centre.

places.name: Shropshire
places.description: A large, rural county on the Welsh border, home to Ironbridge Gorge — the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution and a UNESCO World Heritage Site — alongside rolling hills and market towns like Shrewsbury and Ludlow.

places.name: Telford and Wrekin
places.description: A New Town in Shropshire built around historic villages, named for engineer Thomas Telford, sitting near the Wrekin hill and the Ironbridge Gorge birthplace of industry.

lists.name: Somerset
lists.description: Somerset is a predominantly rural county in South West England known for the Somerset Levels, Mendip Hills, cider orchards and historic towns. Bath is internationally renowned for its Roman and Georgian heritage, while Wells, Taunton and Glastonbury contribute to the county's rich history.

places.name: Bath and North East Somerset
places.description: A district centred on the Georgian city of Bath, famous for its Roman baths, honey-coloured stone crescents, and status as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

places.name: Mendip
places.description: A district in Somerset named for the Mendip Hills, home to Wells, England's smallest city, and the dramatic limestone gorge at Cheddar.

places.name: North Somerset
places.description: A district covering the seaside resort of Weston-super-Mare and countryside on the edge of the Mendip Hills.

places.name: Sedgemoor
places.description: A district in Somerset covering the Somerset Levels wetlands and the town of Bridgwater, site of the 1685 Battle of Sedgemoor, the last pitched battle fought on English soil.

places.name: South Somerset
places.description: A rural district around the market town of Yeovil, with rolling hills, historic Montacute House, and the picturesque town of Sherborne just over the Dorset border.

places.name: Taunton Deane
places.description: A former district in Somerset centred on the county town of Taunton, historically a centre for the wool and cider trades.

places.name: West Somerset District
places.description: A rural, coastal district covering part of Exmoor National Park and the seaside town of Minehead, known for dramatic moorland and the West Somerset Railway heritage line.

lists.name: South Downs Way
lists.description: Hike

badge.name: South Downs Way
badge.description: Walk the full South Downs Way.

lists.name: South Yorkshire
lists.description: South Yorkshire is a metropolitan county in northern England centred on Sheffield and a network of former industrial towns. It has a strong steel and manufacturing heritage, while the western part reaches into the Peak District's dramatic landscapes.

places.name: Sheffield
places.description: A South Yorkshire city famous worldwide for steel production, particularly cutlery, now reinvented with extensive green space — a third of the city sits within the Peak District — and a strong music heritage.

places.name: Barnsley
places.description: A former coal-mining town in South Yorkshire, its identity still shaped by that industrial heritage even as the pits have long closed. Known for its market, Elsecar Heritage Centre, and strong working-class cultural pride.

places.name: Doncaster
places.description: A South Yorkshire town with deep railway heritage, home to the St Leger Stakes, the world's oldest classic horse race, run at Doncaster Racecourse since 1776.

places.name: Rotherham
places.description: A former steel and coal town in South Yorkshire, home to Magna Science Adventure Centre inside a converted steelworks, and close to Wentworth Woodhouse, one of England's largest private houses.

lists.name: Staffordshire
lists.description: Staffordshire is a centrally located county in the West Midlands known for its industrial heritage, pottery, ceramics and historic towns. Stafford, Stoke-on-Trent and Tamworth are major centres, while Cannock Chase and the Staffordshire Moorlands provide extensive countryside.

places.name: Lichfield
places.description: A cathedral city in Staffordshire notable for its three-spired medieval cathedral and as the birthplace of Samuel Johnson, compiler of one of the first English dictionaries.

places.name: Newcastle-under-Lyme
places.description: A market town in Staffordshire distinct from Newcastle upon Tyne, with a history tied to coal mining and pottery, and a well-preserved medieval street layout.

places.name: Staffordshire Moorlands
places.description: A district covering the southern Peak District fringes in Staffordshire, including the pottery town of Leek, known for its textile heritage.

places.name: Tamworth
places.description: A market town in Staffordshire, once the capital of the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia, with a castle dating to the Norman period still standing above the town.

places.name: Cannock Chase
places.description: A district in Staffordshire named for its Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty — one of England's smallest AONBs — a stretch of ancient heathland and forest that was once a royal hunting ground.

places.name: East Staffordshire
places.description: A district around the brewing town of Burton upon Trent, long known as the historic centre of English beer production thanks to its mineral-rich water.

places.name: South Staffordshire
places.description: A rural district surrounding the Black Country conurbation, with villages and countryside offering a green contrast to the industrial towns nearby.

places.name: Stafford
places.description: The county town of Staffordshire, with a partly timber-framed medieval centre and strong historical ties to shoemaking.

places.name: Stoke-on-Trent
places.description: The heart of England's ceramics industry, historically known as 'The Potteries' for the six towns that merged to form the city, including famous names like Wedgwood and Spode.

lists.name: Suffolk
lists.description: Suffolk is a largely rural county in eastern England known for farmland, picturesque villages, medieval wool towns and a long North Sea coastline. Ipswich is the main urban centre, while Bury St Edmunds, Southwold and Aldeburgh are notable historic and cultural destinations.

places.name: Mid Suffolk
places.description: A rural district of Suffolk market towns and villages, including Stowmarket and Eye, known for timber-framed buildings and gentle farmland.

places.name: Babergh
places.description: A rural district in Suffolk known for its picture-postcard wool towns like Lavenham, with some of England's best-preserved medieval timber-framed buildings.

places.name: Forest Heath
places.description: A former district in Suffolk covering Newmarket, the historic headquarters of British horse racing and home to the National Horseracing Museum.

places.name: Ipswich
places.description: The county town of Suffolk and one of England's oldest continuously inhabited towns, with a waterfront marina built from its historic docks.

places.name: West Suffolk
